acs.text: A runbook in the repo describes the attended first apply and the DNS cut-over from the current page. ([EN-002](https://github.com/jakubigla/personal-site/blob/main/.xpm/catalog/en/EN-002.md) AC6)
acs.raw_artifact:
1	# Runbook: first apply and DNS cut-over
     2	
     3	Every Terraform apply is attended (ADR-0010). Nothing here runs in CI and CI holds no AWS
     4	credential for these roots. You need: AWS credentials for the owner's account with rights to
     5	create S3, CloudFront, ACM, Route 53 records and Budgets; Terraform 1.10 or newer; the
     6	Route 53 hosted zone for `jacops.pl`, which already exists.
     7	
     8	The bucket names (`jacops-pl-terraform-state`, `jacops-pl-site`) are global; if S3 reports one
     9	taken, change it in `infra/bootstrap/main.tf` (and the `backend` block in
    10	`infra/environments/prod/main.tf`) or in the `site_hosting` module call, and commit that.
    11	
    12	## 1. Check the code locally
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	terraform fmt -check -recursive infra
    16	infra/policies/test.sh
    17	```
    18	
    19	## 2. Bootstrap the state bucket (once)
    20	
    21	```bash
    22	cd infra/bootstrap
    23	terraform init
    24	terraform apply
    25	```
    26	
    27	Its own state stays in `terraform.tfstate` in this directory. It is gitignored: keep it, never
    28	commit it. The bucket is versioned, encrypted, private and has `prevent_destroy`.
    29	
    30	## 3. First apply of the hosting root
    31	
    32	The current page is served by the old 2021 distribution, which holds the `jacops.pl` and
    33	`www.jacops.pl` aliases. CloudFront refuses to create a distribution with an alias another
    34	distribution already uses (`CNAMEAlreadyExists`), so the first apply runs with
    35	`serve_domain=false`: the distribution gets no aliases and the apex and www records are left
    36	alone. Everything else, the bucket policy included, is created.
    37	
    38	```bash
    39	cd infra/environments/prod
    40	terraform init
    41	terraform plan -var serve_domain=false -out=hosting.tfplan
    42	```
    43	
    44	Read the plan. Expect new: the site bucket, its public access block, ownership, encryption and
    45	policy, the CloudFront distribution with no aliases, origin access control, response headers
    46	policy, the router function, the certificate and its validation records, and the budget.
    47	Expect no apex or www record, and no WAF, NAT gateway, compute or logging resource. Then:
    48	
    49	```bash
    50	terraform apply hosting.tfplan
    51	```
    52	
    53	The apply creates the validation records, waits for the certificate and creates the
    54	distribution. The old page stays live: nothing it uses is touched.
    55	
    56	Confirm the budget subscription: AWS emails the contact address; open it if it asks you to
    57	confirm.
    58	
    59	## 4. Upload the site and check the new distribution
    60	
    61	Upload the built site to the bucket named by `terraform output site_bucket` (the deploy job
    62	does this once its role exists), then invalidate if needed. Check the distribution on its own
    63	`*.cloudfront.net` name (it has no alias yet, so a `jacops.pl` host header would reach the old
    64	distribution):
    65	
    66	```bash
    67	H=$(terraform output -raw distribution_domain)
    68	curl -sI https://"$H"/ | head -20             # 200 with the new site
    69	curl -sI https://"$H"/does-not-exist        # 404 with the custom page
    70	curl -sI http://"$H"/                         # 301 to https
    71	```
    72	
    73	You should see `strict-transport-security`, `content-security-policy`,
    74	`x-content-type-options`, `referrer-policy` and `x-frame-options` on every response. Do not go
    75	on until all three answer as shown.
    76	
    77	## 5. Cut-over: move the aliases, then the records
    78	
    79	The cut-over is the alias move. `aws cloudfront associate-alias` moves an alias from the old
    80	distribution to the new one in one call; the new one's certificate covers both names. From
    81	that moment CloudFront serves the alias from the new distribution, even to clients whose DNS
    82	still points at the old one, so the records can follow without downtime.
    83	
    84	1. Note the old state so the move can be reversed:
    85	
    86	   ```bash
    87	   ZONE=$(aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name jacops.pl \
    88	     --query 'HostedZones[0].Id' --output text)
    89	   aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id "$ZONE" > old-records.json
    90	   OLD=<old distribution id>     # aws cloudfront list-distributions; the one with the aliases
